ES.label: S&P 500 Fut
ES.source: S&P 500 E-mini, 7759.50, +4.75 points, Perplexity consolidated feed stamped 11:02 UTC in a snapshot pulled 11:12 UTC, priced off Thursday's 7754.75 settle. Overnight range 7748.25 to 7764.50 - a sixteen-point band, which is close to the narrowest overnight range this board has printed in a month. That stillness is the signal: the August employment report lands at 8:30 this morning and the market has stopped taking positions into it. Thursday's CASH close was 7747.71, up 1.058% from 7666.60 - the second consecutive green session and the largest single-day gain since mid-August. NOT ATH: the cash index sits -0.658% below its record close of 7798.99 set 8/13/26 and -0.883% below the 7816.70 record intraday high from the same session. It is close - about half a percent of upside would do it - but it has not done it, and Thursday's high of 7756.76 was still 60 points short of the record high. The two-session recovery has retraced essentially all of the hawkish scare that dominated the start of the week.

NQ.label: Nasdaq 100 Fut
NQ.source: Nasdaq 100 E-mini, 29660.75, +136.00 points, +0.46%, consolidated feed stamped 11:01 UTC off Thursday's 29524.75 settle. Overnight range 29482.00 to 29697.25. Note the divergence from the S&P contract, which is flat: the Nasdaq is the only major US future making a real move overnight, and it is being carried by the Thursday-night software earnings cohort rather than by anything macro. Thursday's CASH close was 29482.32, up 1.163% from 29143.33. NOT ATH: -3.843% below the 6/2/26 record close of 30660.60 and -4.161% below the 6/3/26 record high of 30762.20. Three months after the June high the Nasdaq 100 has still not made a new record, and the gap has narrowed by less than a point of percentage over the last week.

SOX.label: Philadelphia Semis
SOX.source: Polygon daily bar, Thursday cash settle, +12.88 points, +0.114%. This is the most informative number on the equity board and the shape matters more than the level. Semis rose one-tenth of a percent on a day the Nasdaq 100 rose 1.16% and the Dow rose 1.18% - a full percentage point of underperformance. But the index traded as low as 11056.38 intraday, roughly 2.5% down, and closed near its session high of 11371.33, so this was a morning shock almost entirely repaired rather than steady weakness. The cause is single-name and identifiable: Broadcom, the heaviest weight in the index, fell 2.74% to $357.16 on its Q4 gross-margin guide after Wednesday night's report. NOT ATH, and not close - the index is -22.43% below its record close of 14634.72 set 6/22/26. Broadcom traded back up about 1.2% overnight, which would mechanically reverse much of the drag if it holds.

DJI.label: Dow Jones Ind
DJI.source: Polygon daily bar, Thursday cash settle, +624.16 points, +1.177%. The best of the four US boards for a second consecutive session, which is a consistent pattern worth naming: the rate-sensitive, low-duration index is leading a rally that is being driven by falling rate expectations rather than by earnings. NOT ATH: -1.220% below the record close of 54349.12 set 8/5/26. The Russell 2000 gained 0.51% to 2968.27 and the Nasdaq Composite 1.397% to 26584.06, so breadth was genuine but tilted to large-cap. Every one of the four boards is now green over two sessions and none of them is at a record.

VIX.label: VIX
VIX.source: Cboe VIX, Thursday settle, down 0.88 points or -5.79% from Wednesday's 15.20. Thursday's intraday high was 15.44. This is a volatility index at 14.32 going into a payrolls print, and that pairing deserves to be stated plainly rather than buried: the options market is pricing an unusually quiet reaction to the single most consequential scheduled data release of the week. Two sessions ago the VIX was above 16 on a global rates shock; it has now given the entire move back and sits at the bottom of the 14 to 16 band that has contained it since late July. The Nasdaq analogue VXN settled 20.16, down 4.32% from 21.07, also falling. Freshness discipline: Polygon again served a same-day pre-open VIX bar at 14.16 this morning, which was rejected in favour of Thursday's settle.

US10Y.label: US 10Y Yield
US10Y.source: US 10-year Treasury yield, 4.761%, down 0.1 basis point from Thursday's 4.762% close, overnight range 4.746% to 4.780%, page stamped Real-time Data 07:02:12 and verified independently of the 2-year page. Unchanged is the correct description. The long end has stopped moving entirely ahead of 8:30, which is consistent with the flat equity futures and the narrow overnight ranges elsewhere. Read this tile as a LEVEL: the percentage-change figure shown is the change in the yield itself, not a basis-point move, so a tenth of a basis point renders as a very small percentage rather than as nothing. The yield is now roughly 3 basis points below where it started the week, having been at a one-year high on Tuesday.

US2Y.label: US 2Y Yield
US2Y.source: US 2-year Treasury yield, 4.365%, down 2.1 basis points from Thursday's 4.386%, overnight range 4.361% to 4.376%. The front end continues to fall faster than the long end, which is the correct signature for a dovish repricing: the 2-year is the Fed-expectations instrument and it has now dropped four sessions in a row. That puts 2s10s at roughly 39.6 basis points, essentially unchanged from Thursday. Freshness note: this page's own clock read 08:06:44 at a wall-clock near 07:10 ET, the known one-hour-ahead artifact on some Investing.com pages. The quote itself is fresh - its stated previous close of 4.386 matches Thursday's official close and its overnight range is disjoint from it - so the clock is wrong and the price is right.

WTI.label: WTI Crude
WTI.source: WTI front-month crude, $90.54, -0.83% from Thursday's $91.30 settle, overnight range $90.37 to $92.16. Contract month re-verified independently this run rather than assumed, per the standing rule after the session when WTI front was October while Brent front was November. Crude is finally giving something back after the week's run, and it is doing so on a night when the Middle East was active rather than quiet: Iran struck US bases in Kuwait and the UAE on Thursday morning and the US disabled three vessels overnight. Both benchmarks are still on track for their strongest weekly gain since mid-July, which is the point - the escalation was priced in earlier this week and the overnight tape is fading it, not extending it.

BRENT.label: Brent Crude
BRENT.source: Brent front-month, $95.01, -0.53% from Thursday's $95.52, overnight range $94.82 to $96.22. Contract month confirmed separately from WTI. The Brent-WTI spread sits near $4.47, marginally wider than Thursday and still consistent with a supply-side rather than demand-side bid. Brent above $95 with the VIX at 14.32 remains the standing tension on this board: the equity market has priced Gulf risk down to almost nothing while the physical crude market has not. The live tail risk is specific and was restated inside the window - Israel's defence minister said Israel would target Iranian energy infrastructure if Iran attacked Israel. No verified war-risk insurance datapoint exists in the window, so none is published here.

GOLD.label: Gold
GOLD.source: Gold futures, $4,518.60, -0.47% from Thursday's $4,539.90, overnight range $4,506.60 to $4,537.80. Gold rose roughly 2.4% on Thursday as the hike odds collapsed and is giving back a fifth of that overnight. Silver is down 0.49% at $67.37 alongside, so this is the whole precious complex easing together rather than a gold-specific move. Note the cross-check that matters: the dollar index is DOWN 0.53% at 99.06 overnight while gold is also down. A softer dollar with softer gold is not the debasement configuration that held earlier in the week - it reads as position-trimming ahead of 8:30 rather than as a change in the underlying trade.

BTC.label: Bitcoin
BTC.source: Bitcoin, $81,128.99, -0.18%, overnight range $80,622.66 to $81,392.30, from the consolidated crypto feed and cross-checked against the Polygon X:BTCUSD daily series, which puts Thursday's close at $81,263.99 against $77,305.10 Wednesday. That is the number to understand on this tile: Bitcoin rose 5.12% on Thursday, and essentially all of it happened after Governor Waller spoke at 8:30. It has given back nothing overnight. More than $415mn of short positions were liquidated as the price took out $81,000, so a forced-covering component is well supported even though the various venue tallies disagree on magnitude. The instrument is trading as a dollar-liquidity asset rather than as a risk asset, and it remains well below its own highs.

EURJPY.label: EUR/JPY
EURJPY.source: Euro-yen, 181.69, UP 0.29% from 181.17, overnight range 180.60 to 181.96. The direction has reversed and that needs saying clearly rather than smoothing over: after two sessions of sharp yen strength, the yen gave a little back overnight. Aussie-yen is up 0.48% and dollar-yen up 0.32% at 156.34, so it is consistent across all three crosses. But the week's trend is intact and the levels are what matter - dollar-yen traded as strong as 155.25 for the yen in Friday morning trade, the strongest in a month and essentially a retest of the post-July-intervention high near 155.20, before retreating. The yen is still on track for a weekly gain of roughly 2.2%, its biggest since late July.

AUDJPY.label: AUD/JPY
AUDJPY.source: Aussie-yen, 112.57, up 0.48% from 112.03, overnight range 111.83 to 112.79. Read against Aussie-dollar, which is essentially unchanged overnight at -0.01%: so this is yen weakness rather than Australian strength, the mirror image of Wednesday and Thursday. Applying the funding-squeeze test explicitly, as required: the crosses are UP 0.3% to 0.5%, so the first condition does not even arise - a carry unwind cannot be running while the carry crosses rally. VXN is 20.16 and falling, equity futures are flat to higher, and the dollar is broadly soft. Verdict: no funding squeeze, and the two-day yen repricing has paused rather than broken. This remains the instrument to watch, because Japan's top currency diplomat said Friday he is in constant contact with US authorities, which keeps two-way intervention risk live.
